newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government bonds firm on interbank rate.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government bonds firm on interbank rate.

text.p: Singapore government bonds closed firmer across the board on Wednesday in moderate trade on interbank and retail interest, dealers said.
"Bond prices were marked up slightly today following a small fall in the interbank rate. Treasury bill yields were slightly lower. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
Among bonds, April 1999 ended at S$98.63/98.68 compared with Tuesday's close of S$98.53/98.58, May 2002 at S$99.64/99.69 against S$99.53/99.58 and June 2003 at S$94.68/94.73 from S$94.57/94.62.
The overnight interbank offered rate fell to 2-1/8 2 percent versus Tuesday's 2-5/8 2-1/2 percent.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 2.63/2.58 percent against Tuesday's yield of 2.83/2.78 percent and one-year at a yield of 2.63/2.58 percent from 2.67/2.62 percent.
